_about: Sir Philip Sidney. Bloom's Western Canon (1994) lists: An Apology for Poetry; Astrophel and Stella; The Countess of Pembroke's Arcadia. Bloom addition 2026-11-03 under Adam's Bloom-only ruling; each row is US public domain (title page, Gutenberg header or IA metadata read, recorded in _bloom).

sidney-p: Sir P.S.: His Astrophel and Stella
sidney-defence-poesie-poems: A Defence of Poesie and Poems

sidney-countess-pembroke-arcadia.year: 1907 (PG header: 'Original publication: George Routledge and Sons, 1907'; editor Ernest A. Baker)
sidney-countess-pembroke-arcadia.case: Bloom lists the Arcadia; PG 70854 is Baker's edition of the composite Arcadia.
sidney-countess-pembroke-arcadia.note: Nothing of Sir Philip Sidney is held (machine matched other Sidneys).

sidney-p.year: 1591 (PG text reproduces title: 'At London, Printed for Thomas Newman. Anno Domini 1591')
sidney-p.case: PG 56375 is a transcription of the first (Newman 1591) quarto.
sidney-p.note: Old spelling. PG 1962 (Defence of Poesie and Poems) also contains the sonnets in a modernized text.

sidney-defence-poesie-poems.year: 1891 (PG credits: 'Transcribed from the 1891 Cassell & Company edition')
sidney-defence-poesie-poems.case: The Apology for Poetry = The Defence of Poesie; PG 1962 is Henry Morley's Cassell's National Library edition.
